description: Semiconductor photodetector: a PN/PIN junction (or its avalanche, Geiger, position-sensing, or segmented variants) that converts incident light into a photocurrent. Covers silicon PIN/PN photodiodes (UV/visible/NIR), avalanche photodiodes (APD), silicon photomultipliers (SiPM/MPPC), InGaAs photodiodes (telecom NIR), position-sensitive detectors (PSD), and quadrant/segmented detectors. It reuses the LED/laser-diode optical wavelength vocabulary but INVERTED - the emitter's marquee is optical watts out per drive amp (W/A), the detector's is amps of photocurrent out per incident optical watt (A/W responsivity). Out of scope as separate families: LEDs and laser diodes (emitters, already shipped); PHOTOTRANSISTORS (a light-driven BJT whose headline is a nonlinear light current at a stated illuminance/irradiance, not an A/W responsivity); integrated ambient-light-sensor / photodiode-amplifier ICs (sensor systems with supply, output, and often digital interfaces); optocouplers (emitter+detector systems); camera image sensors / photodiode-array ICs; and solar cells (energy devices). Detectivity D* (Jones = cm.sqrtHz/W) is intentionally omitted for this Si/near-IR scope - it is derivable from NEP and area, and datasheets here lead with NEP; a future extended-IR / thermal-detector slice (2-3 um InGaAs, PbS/PbSe, pyroelectric) that makes D* its headline would need a new m.sqrtHz/W unit. Synthesized from a 20-datasheet corpus across Hamamatsu, Thorlabs, ams-OSRAM, Vishay, Excelitas, onsemi/SensL, Laser Components, First Sensor, and Marktech.

parameters.name: Responsivity (photosensitivity)
parameters.hint: The photocurrent produced per watt of incident optical power, in A/W - the detector's defining spec and the literal reciprocal of a laser's W/A slope efficiency (a printed mA/mW is the identical number). Wavelength-dependent: array over the LAMBDA (wavelength) axis for the spectral-response curve, and attach the wavelength (usually the peak, or a stated line like 1550 nm) as a condition. ~0.5-0.7 A/W for a Si PIN near its peak, ~0.9-1.05 A/W for InGaAs at 1550 nm. For an APD, responsivity is quoted at a stated multiplication gain M (attach the M condition) and reaches tens of A/W; do NOT confuse the at-gain (M>1) figure with the intrinsic M=1 value.

parameters.name: Quantum efficiency
parameters.hint: The fraction of incident photons that generate a collected electron-hole pair, in percent (QE = responsivity x 1240 / (lambda_nm x M) x 100). ~70-90% for a good Si/InGaAs detector at its peak. Wavelength-dependent.

parameters.name: Peak sensitivity wavelength
parameters.hint: The wavelength of maximum responsivity, in metres (nm/um normalized: 960 nm is 9.6e-7, 1.55 um is 1.55e-6). Note `m` here is a wavelength, distinct from a physical size (photosensitive_diameter) that also uses `m` - the parameter key carries the distinction.

parameters.name: Spectral response range
parameters.hint: The wavelength band over which the detector responds (usually to the 10% or 50%-of-peak points), in metres - store min = short-wavelength edge, max = long-wavelength edge (320-1100 nm is min 3.2e-7 / max 1.1e-6). Set by the semiconductor bandgap (Si ~1100 nm cutoff, InGaAs ~1700 nm).

parameters.name: Cutoff wavelength
parameters.hint: The long-wavelength 50%-responsivity cutoff, in metres (an InGaAs part's ~1.7 um is 1.7e-6). The bandgap edge; distinct from the spectral_response_range endpoints when a part specifies it separately.

parameters.name: Photosensitive (active) area
parameters.hint: The active (light-sensitive) area, in square metres (mm2 normalized: 7.5 mm2 is 7.5e-6; a large-area 18x18 mm detector is 3.24e-4). A first-class selection parameter - dark current, capacitance, and NEP all scale with it. Use this when a datasheet prints the area as a scalar; for a circular detector that instead prints a diameter, use photosensitive_diameter.

parameters.name: Photosensitive diameter
parameters.hint: The diameter of a circular active area, in metres (um/mm normalized: 0.5 mm is 5e-4, 200 um is 2e-4). The common form for small circular Si/InGaAs detectors; a square/rectangular part uses photosensitive_area instead.

parameters.name: Dark current
parameters.hint: The reverse leakage current in darkness at a stated reverse voltage (attach V_R), in amperes (nA/pA normalized: 10 nA is 1e-8). Array over V_R - it rises steeply near breakdown, and for an APD is quoted at a stated gain M (attach M). Roughly doubles every ~7-8 degC; a datasheet that prints the multiplicative temperature factor as its own row (e.g. TCID = 1.15 times/degC) stores it in dark_current_temperature_factor, not buried here. Sets the low-light detection floor.

parameters.name: Shunt resistance
parameters.hint: The zero-bias junction (parallel) resistance, in ohms (MOhm/GOhm normalized: 125 MOhm is 1.25e8), measured at a small bias (e.g. 10 mV). A precision/low-light photovoltaic-mode spec (higher is better); general-purpose parts often omit it.

parameters.name: Terminal (junction) capacitance
parameters.hint: The junction capacitance at a stated reverse bias and measurement frequency (attach V_R and F), in farads (pF normalized: 70 pF is 7e-11). Falls as reverse voltage widens the depletion region (array over V_R); with the load resistance it sets the detector's bandwidth. Scales with active area.

parameters.name: Reverse voltage (maximum)
parameters.hint: The absolute-maximum reverse (bias) voltage the detector operates at (limitClass absolute_max), in volts. For a PIN this is the operating bias ceiling; for an APD the recommended operating bias sits just below breakdown_voltage - store that recommended bias as operating_voltage with limitClass recommended.

parameters.name: Breakdown voltage
parameters.hint: The reverse voltage at avalanche breakdown (defined at a stated test current, e.g. Id = 100 uA, or by the sqrt(I)-vs-V intercept for a SiPM), in volts - the anchor an APD/SiPM operates relative to (a Si reach-through APD ~200 V, a SiPM ~25 V). Its strong temperature dependence is temperature_coefficient_breakdown_voltage.

parameters.name: Recommended operating (reverse) voltage
parameters.hint: The recommended reverse bias (limitClass recommended), in volts, at which an APD reaches its rated gain or a SiPM its rated overvoltage. Often binned per-unit (an APD ships with a per-device VOP giving M=150 at 25 degC); a SiPM specifies an overvoltage above breakdown_voltage - keep the 'Vbr + N V' form in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Multiplication (avalanche) gain
parameters.hint: The avalanche multiplication factor M - a dimensionless number (unit 1) that scales the primary photocurrent. Array over reverse voltage (it rises steeply toward breakdown); ~100-200 for a linear-mode APD, ~1e6 for a Geiger-mode SiPM. Responsivity, dark current, and bandwidth are all quoted at a stated M.

parameters.name: Gain-bandwidth product
parameters.hint: The product of avalanche gain and -3 dB bandwidth, in hertz (GHz normalized) - a figure of merit for a high-speed APD (the bandwidth falls as gain rises). Some parts tabulate bandwidth per gain point instead.

parameters.name: Excess noise factor
parameters.hint: The excess noise factor F - a dimensionless number (unit 1) by which the avalanche multiplication adds noise beyond ideal, F = k*M + (2 - 1/M)(1 - k). Rises with gain M (array over the M axis); lower is better. Distinct from the material k-factor.

parameters.name: Excess noise k-factor
parameters.hint: The effective ionization-rate ratio k (= beta/alpha) - a dimensionless material constant (unit 1, ~0.02 for a good Si APD, higher for InGaAs) that sets the excess_noise_factor's growth with gain. Lower k means quieter avalanche.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of breakdown voltage
aliases: temperature coefficient of reverse voltage for constant gain
parameters.hint: The drift of breakdown voltage with temperature, in V/degC (a printed mV/degC or V/K is the identical number for a delta: 21.5 mV/degC is 0.0215). Positive; it forces an APD/SiPM bias-compensation loop to hold constant gain over temperature.

parameters.name: Noise current density
parameters.hint: The dark (shot) noise current spectral density, in A/sqrtHz (pA/sqrtHz normalized: 0.1 pA/sqrtHz is 1e-13). The numerator of NEP (NEP = noise_current_density / responsivity); printed mainly on APDs.

parameters.name: Noise equivalent power
parameters.hint: The optical power that produces a signal equal to the noise in a 1 Hz bandwidth, in W/sqrtHz (fW/sqrtHz and pW/sqrtHz normalized: 1.1e-14 W/sqrtHz; 0.04 pW/sqrtHz is 4e-14), at a stated reverse voltage and wavelength (the peak). The detector's sensitivity floor and its headline noise figure; lower is better. Detectivity D* (Jones) is derivable from NEP and area and is not stored.

parameters.name: Rise time
parameters.hint: The 10%-90% output rise time at a stated reverse voltage, load resistance, and wavelength (attach V_R, R_L), in seconds (ns/us normalized: 10 ns is 1e-8). With fall_time and terminal_capacitance it sets the detector's speed; tr = 0.35 / cutoff_frequency.

parameters.name: Fall time
parameters.hint: The 90%-10% output fall time at a stated bias and load, in seconds (ns/us normalized). Pairs with rise_time.

parameters.name: Cutoff frequency (bandwidth)
parameters.hint: The -3 dB electrical bandwidth at a stated reverse voltage and load resistance (attach V_R, R_L), in hertz (MHz/GHz normalized: 500 MHz is 5e8). Set by the RC of terminal_capacitance and the load; for an APD it is quoted at a stated gain.

parameters.name: Short-circuit current
parameters.hint: The photocurrent at zero bias under a stated illumination, in amperes (uA normalized). Because the illumination is heterogeneous across vendors (an irradiance in W/m2, or a photometric illuminance in lux, or a defined light source), keep the exact stimulus (e.g. '100 lx, CIE illuminant A' or 'Ee = 1 mW/cm2, 950 nm') in conditionsVerbatim - it is meaningless without it.

parameters.name: Open-circuit voltage
parameters.hint: The photovoltaic voltage across the unloaded junction under a stated illumination, in volts (mV normalized). Keep the illumination stimulus in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Photon detection efficiency
parameters.hint: For a SiPM/MPPC, the probability that an incident photon at the peak wavelength produces a detected avalanche, in percent (the product of quantum efficiency, fill factor, and avalanche-trigger probability). Rises with overvoltage; quote the overvoltage in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Dark count rate
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the rate of thermally-triggered (dark) avalanche pulses, in hertz (kHz/MHz normalized: 1200 kHz is 1.2e6, 3.4 MHz is 3.4e6), at a stated overvoltage - the Geiger-mode analogue of a PIN's dark current, and the SiPM's noise floor.

parameters.name: Optical crosstalk
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the probability that one microcell avalanche triggers a neighbour via secondary photons, in percent - it adds correlated noise. For a quadrant/segmented detector the same key name is reused for inter-segment crosstalk (put which sense in conditionsVerbatim).

parameters.name: Afterpulsing probability
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the probability that a trapped carrier re-triggers the same microcell after the primary avalanche, in percent - correlated noise that degrades timing/counting.

parameters.name: Number of microcells
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the count of Geiger microcells (unit 1, an integer) - it sets the dynamic range (a cell can only fire once per recharge). Pairs with microcell_size and fill_factor.

parameters.name: Microcell size (pitch)
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the microcell pitch, in metres (um normalized: 35 um is 3.5e-5) - smaller cells give more dynamic range but lower fill factor / PDE.

parameters.name: Fill factor
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the fraction of the active area that is photosensitive (not consumed by trenches/quench resistors), in percent - a direct multiplier on PDE.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of gain
parameters.hint: For a SiPM at fixed bias, the relative drift of gain with temperature - datasheets print it in %/degC; normalize to ppm/degC (x1e4: -0.8 %/degC is -8000 ppm/degC). Driven by the breakdown-voltage tempco; the reason SiPMs need bias compensation.

parameters.name: Position resolution
parameters.hint: For a position-sensitive detector (PSD), the smallest resolvable change in the light spot's position, in metres (um normalized: 0.7 um is 7e-7), at a stated photocurrent and bandwidth. The PSD's headline spec.

parameters.name: Position detection error
parameters.hint: For a PSD, the deviation between the detected and true spot position across the active area, in metres (um normalized: +/-150 um is 1.5e-4) - the linearity of the position readout, at a stated wavelength, bias, and spot size.

parameters.name: Interelectrode resistance
parameters.hint: For a PSD, the resistance of the resistive position-sensing layer between opposing electrodes, in ohms (kOhm normalized: 7 kOhm is 7000) - it sets the position-signal division and the detector noise/speed.

parameters.name: Saturation photocurrent
parameters.hint: For a PSD, the maximum photocurrent before the position readout saturates, in amperes (uA normalized), at a stated bias and load.

parameters.name: Segment gap width
parameters.hint: For a quadrant/segmented detector, the width of the insensitive gap between adjacent segments, in metres (um normalized: 110 um is 1.1e-4) - it sets the position dead-band at the center.

parameters.name: Segment matching (uniformity)
parameters.hint: For a quadrant/segmented detector, the maximum spread of photocurrent (or dark current) between segments under uniform illumination, in percent (+/-5%) - a small mismatch is what makes the null-balance position measurement accurate.

parameters.name: Power dissipation
parameters.hint: The maximum power dissipation (limitClass absolute_max), in watts (mW normalized: 100 mW is 0.1).

parameters.name: Thermal resistance, junction to ambient
parameters.hint: Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance, in degC/W (or K/W). Matters for cooled/large-area detectors.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of responsivity
parameters.hint: The relative drift of responsivity with temperature - datasheets print it in %/degC or ppm/degC (a printed %/degC normalizes x1e4). Small near the peak, steep near the band edge (a Si part rises fast beyond ~1000 nm).

parameters.name: Operating temperature range
parameters.hint: The ambient temperature range over which the part operates (recommended), in degC. Store min/max bounds.

parameters.name: Storage temperature range
parameters.hint: The non-operating storage temperature range (limitClass absolute_max), in degC. Store min/max bounds.

parameters.name: Dark-current temperature factor
parameters.hint: The multiplicative factor by which dark current rises per degC - a dimensionless number (unit 1, ~1.03-1.15, i.e. dark current roughly doubles every 7-8 degC). Printed as its own tabulated row (TCID / delta-TID) on many Si/InGaAs detectors. Store the printed per-degC multiplier; the 'per degC' basis is kept in conditionsVerbatim (there is no 1/degC unit, and this is NOT a small additive tempco).

parameters.name: Forward current (maximum)
parameters.hint: The absolute-maximum forward current the detector survives (limitClass absolute_max), in amperes (mA/uA normalized) - a stress rating, distinct from any photocurrent. A datasheet may give an average and a single-peak value (store the average, note the peak in verbatim).

parameters.name: Reverse current (maximum)
parameters.hint: The absolute-maximum reverse current rating (limitClass absolute_max), in amperes - a stress limit, distinct from dark_current (which is the characterized leakage). Do NOT confuse the two: same symbol space, different limitClass.

parameters.name: Soldering temperature
parameters.hint: The maximum soldering/lead temperature (limitClass absolute_max), in degC (leaded parts ~200-260 for a few seconds; a ceramic MPPC ~350 for 3 s or ~240 peak reflow) - keep the time and method (hand/reflow, JEDEC MSL) in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Microcell quench resistor
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the resistance in series with each Geiger microcell that quenches (halts) the avalanche, in ohms (kOhm normalized: 500 kOhm is 5e5). With the microcell capacitance it sets the microcell_recovery_time.

parameters.name: Microcell recovery time
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the recharge time constant of a fired microcell (tau = Rq x Cd), in seconds (ns normalized: 95 ns is 9.5e-8) - it bounds the maximum count rate before pile-up.

parameters.name: Single photon time resolution
parameters.hint: For a SiPM, the timing jitter (FWHM) on a single detected photon, in seconds (ps normalized: 200 ps is 2e-10) - the headline for time-of-flight / PET / LiDAR. Distinct from rise_time/fall_time (the analog pulse edges).

parameters.name: Excess noise index
parameters.hint: The exponent x in the F = M^x formulation of excess noise - a dimensionless number (unit 1, ~0.2-0.7), the common alternate to the k-factor especially on InGaAs APDs that tabulate x directly. Use excess_noise_k_factor when a part gives k instead.
